◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈━◈
It's been a busy period behind the scenes and it's about time for a progress update so here we go!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36210911/1227d09630ed504d6357ade5b2b214794ee31c77.png[/img]

[h2]Godot Progress & Coding[/h2]

> The most complex coding tasks are out of the way! [ <3 Godot ]
> We're keeping the new Combat / Inventory system under wraps for now, but the functionality is mostly completed (although all graphics are placeholder).
> The most difficult / main parts of the 'Visual novel scene system' is essentially completed (just need to add easy/quick stuff, e.g. code for playing music etc...)
> Basic functionality for most screens have been ported over from the Java version.

> We've also been experimenting with new possibilities in Godot, such as a code based 'jiggle physics' system for characters (rather than a pre-animated jiggle) This will allow for a 'physics-based' boobie jiggle whenever characters move position on screen etc... [i](NOTE: all visuals are placeholder)[/i]


<To see the video, please view our announcement in discord! (link at the end of this post)> 


- Bigger dungeon maps are now easily possible in Godot, with no need for multiple floors.  [i](NOTE: all visuals are placeholder)[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36210911/72032ef16016287162ab950ce8e20fd26af26bae.png[/img]

As mentioned before, Godot has been such a breath of fresh air to work with and progress has been [i]so[/i] much faster than previously in Java. 

Initial testing of the combat system code functionality has been successful, so we're looking to start play-testing the new combat system internally very soon and if all goes well we will be looking to start replacing placeholder art with the goal of making the game presentable for getting external feedback as well.

※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※※
[h2]Character Art / Sex Scenes[/h2]

Previously, the approach to sex scene planning and the totality of the game was a little less than ideal and often led to the need to re-work or re-do scenes at later dates.

So, this time around we're taking a much more structured approach to planning every scene in the game ahead of time and creating storyboards for every scene.

Since this is the perfect time to do so, we're also giving every scene a look over and trying to move them toward a more consistent style and implement some fun additional things we would like to see such as better scene progression and potential internal shots etc. Essentially just giving every scene a quality check and adding/improving where we feel is needed.

Here are a few examples of images from sketched storyboards (as well as a look at both Ignacy and Gull's updated character art above). 

Please do keep in mind though that everything shown is W.I.P. and not finalized!

notes.title: Venture Seas - January 2024 - Progress Report
notes.content:
[h1]Venture Seas is not Dead![/h1]
I'll start this out with a simple and upfront apology, I am genuinely extremely sorry for my lack of communication about Venture Seas.

This was a shitty reaction to stress on my part, which I made worse and worse the longer I was absent.

For those interested in the 'why' of my silence, or more details on my personal situation, feel free to continue reading at the link below.

Otherwise, I hope ya'll can get excited again with me about the new direction for Venture Seas!

[h2][url=https://docs.google.com/document/d/10D07Si9EZLDASU558P7mOiC_jyDVCRLQboqJuI4NMQ0/edit?usp=sharing]Venture Switch: Detailed Apology[/url][/h2]

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

[h2]The Future of Venture Seas[/h2]
One of the [b]biggest issues with Venture Seas[/b] has always been that it was [b]coded using Java[/b] - a language I feel was not suited for my own experience, and the task at hand.

This is a large part of why things that [i]should[/i] be simple (bug fixes or small alterations) can become extremely complex, and tedious, whilst also breaking other systems and code. It also meant that it was extremely difficult to find anyone who could even attempt to assist with the coding - and would want to.

We have done a lot of thinking and planning for the future of venture seas regarding the best way to improve the game and address key areas such as:
> The Gameplay Loop
> Implementing new systems
> Providing an overall better user experience

The current [b]Java implementation has been the biggest roadblock[/b] for achieving this.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36210911/028a8178ece71e078a0ea8231ed802b0f3cb2790.png[/img]

[h2]What is our Solution?[/h2]
Initially I had been looking into Unity, and planning to make that switch however due to events surrounding Unity we have decided the best path forward is to port Venture Seas from [u]Java LibGDX[/u] to [u]Godot[/u]. 

This means that [b]the entire game will be rebuilt[/b] in a new coding language/environment, giving us ample opportunity to fix glaring issues in the game.

[b]I cannot overstate enough just how big an improvement this will be[/b] for reducing bugs and allowing for much quicker changes and alterations to the game based on feedback. 

Originally, Venture Seas was an impulsive, unplanned [i]mess[/i]... Each new 'feature' I added was fueled primarily by my novelty-seeking excitement, which resulted in a bunch of systems which barely integrated together to form a coherent gameplay loop. 

With this new opportunity, as a team, we have undergone detailed planning for how to improve Venture Seas, with extensive design documentation on everything. 

You can expect a more sensible 'gameplay loop', refined user-interface, improved character development/story revisions, and consistent artwork throughout.

I've already been hammering away at the code and recreating the essential systems in Godot.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36210911/028a8178ece71e078a0ea8231ed802b0f3cb2790.png[/img]

[h2]What are the Changes Going Forward?[/h2]

Here is a summary of our plans going forward:
[list]
[*] Venture Seas on a modern game engine (Godot).
[*] Easier bug removal, faster development, and overall better experience for all.
[*] An expanded dev team, with better flexibility.
[*] The project will no longer stall if I am less available, and the coding will no longer be reliant on myself solely.
[*] Our publisher, *CriticalBliss* will be providing access to their resources such as skilled artists to help out on the project (supervised by Toxxy's creative direction).
[*] Gameplay reworks to fit my original intended vision for the game
[*] More user friendly mod support capabilities (you can use the Godot application itself for mod creation)
[*] Improved/extended character development & rewrites.
[*] Less linear main story mode / exploration.
[*] Consistent artwork/quality throughout the adventure.
[/list]
We have a lot of info to cover, so we'll be splitting detailed explanations over time, as all that info can be overwhelming all at once.

[h3]In the Meantime...[/h3]
We will be available in our [b][url=https://discord.gg/C7JKZKS]OFFICIAL DISCORD[/url][/b] to answer any questions you may have, and attempt to resolve any issues/doubts you may have about the project going forward!

We also have shared some previews of our new OST!

Thank you so much for your attention and feedback!

notes.title: Our Plans Going Forward!
notes.content:
In the previous announcement, I talked about changing the development focus.

We polled the community, and the overwhelming majority (79%) agreed that we should pivot away from prioritising new content and instead focus on improving core game systems, resolving gameplay issues, and fixing bugs.

Prior to Steam Early Access, we had the support and feedback of the awesome community following that grew over time alongside the game's development and helped us get to where we are today.

Releasing to Early Access has exposed us to an even wider audience, and along with that has come harsher criticism, and higher expectations.

This feedback was a driver for the aforementioned poll, and having heard your response and weighed our options we've taken the time to internally create a more solid framework of plans for how to improve the game and make it as fun as possible, whilst also addressing issues such as a perceived lack of/difficulty of reaching lewd content.

Early Access may have raised the level of player expectations, but we absolutely plan to exceed them by the time we leave Early Access.

[h1]Steam Reviews[/h1]
Steam reviews are very impactful towards the project, and we are concerned about the recent influx of negative reviews which have raised many valid concerns.

The Recent / All Reviews metric on steam (e.g. Positive / Mixed) can greatly impact the visibility of games on the steam platform and cause projects and games to be lost to the void.

This means that even if a game is significantly improved upon, it may never get the chance it deserves if poor initial review metrics push it to obscurity.

We need to fix these issues NOW, and then push out new content, so people can enjoy the game during the early access, rather than be frustrated by ‘in development’ issues. 

If you do enjoy the game, or are optimistic about its future. Please take the time to leave a review to support us! Feedback helps a lot :)



[h1]Where is the Deepmount Content Update?[/h1]
Earlier this month, all assets and story content for the Deepmount update were completed as planned.

However, we have made a decision against publishing this content update.

The reason for this is primarily that whilst the story/art etc assets are complete, it still takes a significant time investment to code these into the game, and then further time after that to bug test, refine, etc.

Our team had already agreed that the dungeon system in the game had to undergo major changes and so following an overhaul of this system, this work would then be made obsolete - and we would then have to spend that time again implementing the content with the new system.

Instead, we have been planning and experimenting with the new gameplay improvements, and creating the new assets required to implement them.

I apologise to those who were excited to play some new content this month, but please don't fret, as Deepmount Caverns will release in its entirety when the new expeditions system has been implemented.

Here is a teaser of some amazing new Deepmount artwork!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36210911/66ecc4325b2ccb664042c8fd8e46acd3b71b6705.jpg[/img]

[h1]What is going to Change?[/h1]
Based on feedback and reviews, the game is unenjoyable for many users in its current state.

When the concept of the game was first created, I didn't put enough time into planning an overall cohesive structure. Instead, I would create a variety of systems that I thought would be fun and then try to haphazardly 'link' them together into a 'game'.

Venture Seas was also a 'solo development' project for most of its lifetime, and so I rarely had the time to bounce ideas off of other people / developers, in order to refine them.

Now that we have a small team working on the project we are able to work together to improve every aspect of the game.

[h3]New Expedition System[/h3]
[list]
[*] We are majorly reworking the 'dungeon map' / expedition system
[*] Streamlined, more tactical (and fun) experience
[*] Crew progression - power growth throughout the game you can really feel!
[/list]

[h3]Combat[/h3]
[list]
[*] Combat will be improved. Improved feedback (audio and visual), particle effects etc...
[*] There will be changes to the user interface and game balance
[*] New rune card layout, with concise descriptions
[*] New leader and crewman perks, tweaked class system
[*] Combat will be easier to understand, with a dedicated 'step by step' tutorial
[*] Improved visual clarity / context sensitive player cues
[/list]

[h3]Artwork[/h3]
[list]
[*] Toxxy will update existing, dated, art assets, and 'filling gaps' for missing lewd scenes
[*] Animation will be improved on some existing lewd scenes, by our new animator!
[*] All lewd scenes will be repeatable, and also much easier to access
[*] Lewd scenes will be spread evenly throughout the game (no more dry spells!)
[/list]

[h3]Content Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] Existing story content will be refined, and reworked slightly to fit new changes
[*] Each major character on ship will have a full dating progression (with lewd scenes)
[*] Notifications to lead player towards ‘missed/available’ content (especially lewd stuff)
[/list]

[h3]Bugs and Issues[/h3]
[list]
[*] The game will be easier to understand, without the need for 'walls of text' tutorials
[*] Many older blocks of code will be updated to latest standards
[*] Removing bad code with potential for issues
[*] Every aspect of the game will be balanced AS IS, accounting for future content.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36210911/fa46e0e3cbb86c9842d1083a8495ab4964cc9ff8.png[/img]

[h1]When is the next build release?[/h1]
The goal at the moment is to provide the players with an enjoyable experience during early access, achieved through building a stronger foundation, which can then be further tweaked and expanded.

However, transforming the current systems into this new foundation will take a significant amount of time and effort. Please keep in mind that we are not a large studio.

I can only give a rough estimate of how long this will take, but I would expect upwards of 2-3 months.

This is a lot more time between updates than the players may be used to, but we need the time to get this right, and we believe that it will pay dividends in future as new content is added on to a more refined base.

After this build, the game should be in a golden state where we will be releasing content patches and minor improvements until final release.
